the catalysts with the high Co/Al moly ratios and low calcination temperatures have the good catalytic activity for acetone.
the catalytic performance of acetone oxidation over Co-based catalyst is influenced by the Co/Al ratios and calcination temperature.

the effect of Co/Al and calcination temperatures of the catalysts on acetone oxidation.
the influence of the Co/AL molar ratio and calcination temperatures on the catalytic activity of acetone.
the preparation of CoAlO-500 catalyst with the highest acetone conversion of 98.5% at 300 °C and 100% at 325 °C, and the highest selectivity of 100% at all temperatures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Co/Al ratio and the calcination temperature of CoAlOx have a great influence on the catalytic oxidation of acetone.
the Co-based catalysts with 5:1 molar ratio and calcination temperature of 300 °C are more suitable for acetone oxidation.
Co/Al molybdate catalysts derived from layered hydrotalcites with different calcination temperature and Co/Al mols ratio are promising candidates for acetone oxidation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
5:1 catalysts calcined at 300 °C and 200 °C had better catalytic performance for the oxidation of acetone.
CoAlO-500 catalysts were not the optimal catalyst for acetone oxidation due to the poor crystallinity, low surface Co3+/ Co2+ molar, and low temperature reduciblity of the catalyst.
CoAlO-500 catalyst with 5:1 molar ratio of Co/Al exhibited the best catalytic performance for oxidation of acetone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the catalysts derived from layer hydrotalctite precursors with different synthetic composition and calcination temperatures are efficient catalysts for acetone oxidation.
it is possible to obtain a catalyst with high catalytic activity for acetone oxidation through adjusting the synthetic conditions.
the Co/Al = 5:1 and calcination at 200 °C is an optimal condition for the acetone oxidation over CoAlO catalyst.
